unlock.title: Unlock Quant
unlock.description: Enter your keystore passphrase to access your messages.
unlock.placeholder: Your passphrase (leave empty if none was set)

unlock.title: Session expired
unlock.description: Your session expired. Enter your keystore passphrase (leave empty if none was set) to continue.
unlock.reauthHint: If your server session expired too, enter your password below to log in again. Leave it empty to only unlock the keystore.
unlock.reauthNeeded: The server rejected the stored token — enter your account password to log in again. Your keystore passphrase was already verified and is still in the form.
unlock.noIdentity: No user found to unlock: there is no keystore on this device. Please log in again via the login page.
unlock.emailLocked: Email is locked to your account

newChat.title: New chat
newChat.description: Enter the UUID of the user you want to chat with. (Email-based invites are not supported in MVP — see backend report #01.)

newGroup.title: New group
newGroup.e2eWarning: Group E2E encryption is incomplete in MVP. The creator's own public key is used as the group key (see report #02). Adding members requires a separate API call — not yet implemented.

settings.title: Settings
settings.keysMismatch: MISMATCH — re-run key setup on this device
settings.logoutConfirmText: You can log back in with your passphrase. Check the box below to also remove your keystore from this device.
settings.logoutEraseData: Erase all data on this device for this user
settings.pushDenied: Notification permission was denied — enable it in your system/browser settings and try again.
settings.pushNoVapid: Push is not configured on the server (missing VAPID key).
settings.pushUnsupported: This browser does not support Web Push (no Service Worker or PushManager) — notifications only work while the app is open.
settings.pushSubscribeFailed: The browser could not subscribe to the push service. This happens in ungoogled-chromium and builds without Google keys — Web Push is impossible there, notifications only work while the app is open. You may try again.

chat.peerNoKeyDescription: {{email}} hasn't set up end-to-end encryption yet. Messages you send from this device will be encrypted to yourself only — they won't be readable by the recipient until they generate or import a key.

createKeystore.title: Create secure keystore
createKeystore.description: Before you can send encrypted messages, we need to create a keystore file on this device. It holds your server access token (and optionally a PGP private key), protected by a passphrase.
createKeystore.keystoreWarning: The keystore is encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305. If you forget this passphrase, your encrypted history becomes unrecoverable. There is no password reset.
createKeystore.pgpDescription: PGP is only required to encrypt and decrypt messages. If you skip it now, you'll be logged in but the chat composer will stay disabled until you set up a key later via /setup-key.
createKeystore.pgpSeparatePassphrase: Use a different passphrase for the PGP key
createKeystore.importArmoredPlaceholder:
-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----
...
-----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----
createKeystore.skipDescription: A keystore with no PGP key will be created. You'll be able to browse chats and read messages that are already in the clear, but you won't be able to send or receive encrypted messages until you set up a PGP key via /setup-key.
createKeystore.algorithmHelp: ECC is fast (~100 ms) and recommended for modern clients. RSA 4096 is slower (~3-5 s) and only needed for compatibility with very old PGP software (GPG < 2.3).

errors.pgpPassphraseEmpty: PGP passphrase cannot be empty when the checkbox is on
errors.importInvalidArmor: Pasted text does not look like a PGP private key block
errors.importPassphraseRequired: Passphrase for the imported PGP key is required

setupKey.title: Setup your encryption key
setupKey.passphraseImportLabel: Passphrase (optional — only if your key was encrypted)
setupKey.emptyPassphraseWarning: ⚠ Leaving the passphrase empty means anyone with access to the keystore file can decrypt your private key. Use only on trusted, full-disk-encrypted devices.

generate.description: Generate a new PGP key pair. The private key is stored encrypted on your device. The public key is uploaded to the server.
generate.algorithmHelp: ECC is fast (≈100 ms) and recommended for modern clients. RSA 4096 is slower (≈3-5 s) but works with old PGP software (GPG < 2.3).

import.description: Paste your ASCII-armored PGP private key:
import.tip: Tip: the block may also contain a public key section — it's used as-is when present.

export.description: Export your encrypted keystore as a .qks.json file for backup:

share.title: Handle with extreme care
share.warning1: Sharing your private key grants full access to your encrypted messages.
share.warning2: Anyone with this key can decrypt everything ever sent to you AND sign messages as you.
share.warning3: Only share with devices YOU OWN. Use a trusted channel.
share.passphrasePlaceholder: Leave empty if the key has no passphrase
share.confirmCheckbox: I understand the risks of sharing my private key
share.qrWarning: QR code may not scan reliably for RSA 4096 keys (too long). Use copy or .asc file instead.
